**Triage findings (verified fresh 2026-11-05):**

1. **Well-formed, self-contained design ticket.** Issue #6017 (wave-2 follow-up from the #5955 prior-art research) scopes the capability *observability* surface cleanly apart from the server-invariants child's budget observability: three audiences (users inspecting granted vs derived-used sets and their changes since last connection; world authors seeing requested-vs-used diffs, inherited library footprints, uncertified-derivation markings; server admins seeing grants in force, per-world capability inventory, moderation-pack provenance), plus history — capability diffs over time as queryable registry facts. "Done" is concrete: an audience×surface matrix with the concrete views per audience.
2. **Context verified live:** programme issue #5955 is OPEN; parent topic issue #5958 (capability model — requested vs discovered-used sets, registry listing) is OPEN. No hard-stop labels on issue #6017; no blocker and no Drew decision needed to start the design.
3. **Ordering recorded:** the matrix is specified *against the registry schema from issue #5958*, whose design is still open — so this design's registry-schema-facing parts follow #5958's capability-model design; if that schema is not settled when the follow-up runs, the follow-up records its assumed schema explicitly rather than silently forking #5958 (same discipline as the other #5955 children). Sibling exception-policy and moderation follow-ups under #5955 own their markings/provenance inputs; this design consumes, not re-decides, them.

**Disposition:** triaged; design work proceeds as the follow-up task named in the addendum. Issue #6017 stays open for it.

## Proposed audience × surface matrix

This is a **read/query view contract**, not a replacement capability model. The live #5958 issue settles the key distinction as `requested` versus `discovered-used`, but does not yet publish canonical field names or a complete registry schema. Keep those names provisional until #5958 settles them. Also preserve its C2 ruling: isolated/no-filesystem/no-network remains the default; additional file/network capability is opt-in, off by default on servers, first-party-published for now, and designed so a future general-enablement decision remains possible.

One distinction the views must make explicit: **requested is not granted**. Show the world-requested set, the analyzer-derived used set, and the effective server/admin grant as separate facts. A requested capability may be denied; a derived-used capability does not itself authorize use.

| Surface | Users (before/during connection) | World authors (their own worlds) | Server admins |
|---|---|---|---|
| Requested capabilities and effective grant | Requested set for the exact release; separately show granted/denied/conditional effective state, scope, and the policy reason. Do not label the request itself as a grant. | Requested set by release, with the effective policy outcome where known; highlight declarations that appear broader than the derived-used set. | Requested set and effective grant side by side, including grant scope and the policy/default that produced it. |
| Derived-used set and certification | Show the derived-used set for the connected release, attributed to the world or dependency where useful. If derivation is absent or invalidated, show **unknown / not certified** and why, never an empty set that looks like “uses nothing.” | Show transitive library footprint and capability origins, plus certification status, analyzer/input version, and the reason for any uncertified result. Consume #5998/#6000 policy; do not redefine which language features invalidate certification. | Per-world derived-used set and certification status; make uncertified worlds filterable and visibly distinct from certified worlds. Do not treat an uncertified result as safe. |
| Changes over time | Since the user’s last-seen registry revision: requested, effective-grant, and derived-used changes separately. Use #5999’s user-meaningful capability classes for re-approval; a used-set change under an unchanged request is visible but is not silently turned into a new grant. | Compare releases/revisions; show added/removed requested and used capabilities, dependency-origin changes, and certification transitions. | Audit changes to requests, effective grants, derivation/certification, and policy for a world or across the server; filter by time, world, and change kind. |
| Inherited library footprint | Concise summary of capability contribution from included libraries, sufficient to explain why the world’s footprint differs from its own direct declarations. | Expand each transitive library and its contribution/origin; retain the aggregate world set while allowing drill-down. | Aggregate and drill down by world and dependency origin; use the same derived set and provenance as the author view. |
| Grants in force and inventory | For the selected world, show what the server currently permits and the scope of that decision before the user connects. | For each owned world, show the request and known deployment grant outcome; do not imply authors can grant server authority. | Fleet inventory by world, requested/used capabilities, certification, and effective grant; show who/what policy supplied each in-force grant and its scope. |
| Moderation-pack provenance | Show the active pack/version and user-visible policy effect when relevant, separate from capability grants. | Show the pack/version attached to each authored world and its configured local parameters/overrides. | Show pack id/version, publisher/signature status, preset, subscribed feed ids/versions and freshness, plus local overrides/exemptions. Consume the data-only pack and signed/versioned-feed inputs in #6005/#6006; moderation provenance is not itself a capability. |

### History as queryable registry facts

The current view should be the latest projection of revisioned facts, not the only retained state. At minimum, a history query needs a world id, monotonically ordered registry/release revision, event time, event kind, and references to the prior/current values (or normalized deltas) for **requested**, **derived-used**, **certification**, and **effective grants**. Record the catalog/schema and analyzer versions needed to interpret those facts; include actor/policy provenance for grant changes. Moderation-pack/feed version changes can be recorded as a separate provenance event. Sets should use stable capability ids, with display labels resolved for the requested catalog version.

Queries should support current state, a revision/time range, and “since revision X,” so #5959’s reconnect notice can ask for exactly the changes since a client last saw the world. The user’s last-seen cursor belongs to the notice/connection state, not in the world’s capability facts. Access must follow the audience scopes above: users only for worlds they may inspect/connect to, authors only their own worlds, and admins within their server authority. Retention policy is not specified here.

### Boundary with #5958

This proposal does **not** change the requested-vs-discovered-used model, capability vocabulary, compilation ceiling, or default/opt-in posture. The one explicit extension point is history: if #5958 settles a current-entry-only schema, observability needs an append-only revision/event history (or equivalent queryable snapshots) keyed to that schema. That is a schema decision for #5958 to accept or reject; this issue must not silently fork its registry. Exact field names and diff classifications remain owned by #5958 and #5999 respectively.
